title: Oswald's planned role and the killing of Officer Tippit

related.note: Both tell Sheehan's account of the plan for Oswald's shot and Tippit's role. Here Oswald shoots at Kennedy, while the story has a deliberate miss to blame Cuba.

plain: In Dallas in 1963, the plan was for Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of shooting President John F. Kennedy, to take his shot, run away, and then be killed by J. D. Tippit, a Dallas police officer who was himself shot dead that day. A lawyer named Dan Sheehan lays out this account to Michels as something he was told, not something he saw. If true, Oswald was meant to be silenced and Tippit was part of the plot rather than a random victim.
